questions.q: In a series circuit with three bulbs, what happens to the other two bulbs if you unscrew one of them?
questions.a: The other two bulbs will immediately go off. A student who says "they stay on" fails to realize that the current path has been physically broken, preventing electricity from completing its loop.

questions.q: Why is a series circuit considered to have only "one path" for electricity?
questions.a: Because the wire connects the components in a single chain from one terminal of the battery to the other. A student who says "the battery only has one terminal" is confusing the path of the wire with the structure of the battery.

questions.q: If you add a third bulb to a series circuit that already has two bulbs and one battery, what happens to the path of the current?
questions.a: The current must now flow through three bulbs instead of two, but it still follows the same single, unbroken path. A student who thinks the current "splits" is incorrectly applying concepts from parallel circuits.

questions.q: If a string of series-connected LED lights is completely dark, but the battery is new, what is the most likely reason?
questions.a: There is a break in the circuit somewhere, such as a loose wire or a burnt-out bulb, which has stopped the flow of current. If a student suggests "the current is too tired," they are using non-scientific reasoning instead of understanding the necessity of a closed loop.

questions.q: Is it better to connect house lights in series or in a different way? Why?
questions.a: It is not better to connect house lights in series because if one light fails, the whole house would go dark. This shows that the student understands the practical limitation of series circuits: the dependency of all parts on each other.

questions.q: Design a simple mental "map" of a series circuit using a battery, a switch, and two bulbs.
questions.a: The map should show a loop starting at the battery, going through the switch, through bulb 1, then bulb 2, and returning to the battery. A poor answer would show multiple loops or branches, which describes a parallel circuit.

questions.q: Fill in the blank: A series circuit is an electrical ______ where components are connected end-to-end, creating one single, continuous path for the electric current to flow.
Fill in the blank: Have you ever noticed a string of small decorative fairy lights where, if one bulb goes out, the whole string stops ______?
What must you be able to do to master this topic?
questions.a: The student must be able to predict that removing or breaking one component in a series circuit will cause all other components in that loop to stop functioning, and explain why this happens by describing the path of the current.

questions.q: Fill in the blank: Have you ever noticed a string of small ______ fairy lights where, if one bulb goes out, the whole string stops glowing?
